costPerTick.machine: Apple M3 Pro, headless, release host

captures.shows: Antes de qualquer animação: três tiles em linha, o status "idle" e os dois botões em opacidade plena; o driver está instalado e ocioso e o React renderizou uma vez.
Durante o spring: o tile laranja parado e os outros dois saindo da linha para a coluna (cerca de 10 e 20 pontos do lugar de origem), status "spring: running", cedo na animação.
Depois do spring: os três tiles em coluna, exatamente onde o Yoga os colocou, status "spring: finished", três renderizações do React.

Durante o ease in / out: o tile laranja que sai, ainda montado, a cerca de 95% de opacidade, os do meio já subindo e o amarelo que entra a cerca de 5%; status "easeInEaseOut: running", cedo na animação.
Depois do ease in / out: o tile laranja removido só no fim, os tiles ciano, roxo e amarelo em coluna, o amarelo opaco, status "easeInEaseOut: finished".

graphical.note: Over eight capture runs the before, spring-end and ease-end frames were byte-identical; the two mid-animation frames differ between runs (three variants of spring-mid, two of ease-mid), because the renderer draws the frame after the one the validation reads. The frames published here are those of run 2.

decisions: The driver is RN's own LayoutAnimationDriver, compiled from react/renderer/animations with no subclass and no copy; no animation logic lives in the host.

The clock RN reads is the pump's frame time in whole milliseconds, handed over at every pump (not only on ticks) because a commit that animates or interrupts pulls between ticks; it never goes back and there is no offset seam.
The in-flight flag is the LayoutAnimationStatusDelegate's, as iOS switches its run loop observer, not the driver's shouldAnimateFrame(), which is also true between configureNext and the commit.

Surfaces get a forwarding MountingOverrideDelegate (RecordingDriver) that records what the driver returns, so a transaction is attributed to the driver exactly, without inferring it from how often the clock is read and without a hook in the runtime.

The oracle recomputes every frame from the clock RN read for each served transaction, with RN's formulas (conversions.h, utils.cpp, LayoutAnimationKeyFrameManager.cpp, ViewPropsInterpolation.h), and never reads a probe verdict; the test feeds it a report whose checks are all marked passed.

Cases whose top-level duration is far longer than their animations (separated) prove the driver, not RN's JS timer, ended the call; the others may be ended by either, and RN calls onAnimationDidEnd once.
Cost per tick was measured with temporary instrumentation and is not a gate.
limitations: Local macOS arm64 evidence; hosted CI and Pages are pending and recorded after the merge; other export targets are separate.
Reduced motion: Platform.isDisableAnimations is undefined under Godot's platform, so configureNext never skips; it is not wired to the AccessibilityInfo setting.

One root at a time: the armed animation is global and the next commit of any surface consumes it. Stopping a root with an animation in flight is covered through its empty commit and the application stop.

Text and Image animate layout only (RN's own limit); type keyboard falls back to linear; easeIn and easeOut run RN's curves without a certificate; delay and initialVelocity are parsed and not exercised.
A deleted view stays mounted, and so reachable by input, for the whole animation, as on RN's platforms; its pointer behavior in Godot is not certified.
Background and resume, behavior under JS load, the mobile exports and hosted macOS and iOS runs are not covered.
The mid-animation captures are the first frame the example's validation accepts, early in the animation, and differ between runs.
The cost per tick has no budget and was measured once on a loaded machine.
No graphical CI: the hosted run is headless.
